A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 16 pages of v2 and 19 pages of v4, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original continual fine-tuning experiments, general-capability evaluations, KL/CoT ablations and RIF-RFT results in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds text-only, model-scale, replay, task-order, runtime and filtering-threshold results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes RIF-RFT selection from maximum rollout reward exceeding τ to mean rollout reward exceeding τ. This changes selection at positive thresholds, although the rules coincide for nonnegative rewards at v4's stated zero default. Section 5.3 still describes the any-rollout rule.

E1.justification: Appendix D.1.1 adds text-only continual training and evaluation on GSM8K mathematical reasoning and USMLE medical-exam questions, extending beyond v2's multimodal continual-training sequence. The original seven downstream datasets and three general-capability benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Table 8 adds SFT with Experience Replay at a 25% replay ratio, evaluated against SFT and GRPO on the 3B three-task sequence. The original Base, MTL-SFT, SFT, ReMax, RLOO and GRPO comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments use Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct and Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, two- and three-task sequences, alternative task orders, 25% replay and thresholds of 0, 0.1 and 0.2. These substantially broaden the evaluation design; the original Section 4.1 settings and accuracy/forgetting metrics are retained.

E4.justification: The existing KL/CoT ablations remain. Appendix D adds model-scale and task-order robustness checks, a filtering-threshold sensitivity study, and a runtime analysis separating filtering overhead from training savings. These address several previously untested robustness and efficiency questions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeat-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The statement about multiple checkpoint restarts for unstable training without KL is retained, and the added tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results, while Tables 6–11 add substantial findings. For example, Table 6 reports GSM8K→USMLE AvgAcc of 73.3% for GRPO versus 64.8% for SFT; Table 10 reports 153.8 hours for GRPO versus 86.62 hours for RIF-RFT including filtering. The aggregate '48.4% of training data' statement disappears, while Table 5's per-task retention fractions remain.

T1.justification: Equation 4 corrects the printed ReMax reward difference from r(x,a)−r(x,a), which cancels, to the difference between sampled-response and greedy-response rewards. Proposition 5.2, the forgetting-risk definitions, technical assumptions and Appendix B proof are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: RFT mitigates forgetting, preserves general capabilities, approaches multitask performance, benefits from implicit reward-variance regularization, and supports efficient instance filtering. The appendix supplies additional evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 changes the explanation for incompetent samples from high-variance noisy gradients to zero or ineffective gradients. It newly acknowledges that filtering can discard samples that become learnable later and explicitly recognizes full-data GRPO's better performance. Appendix D adds interpretations of robustness and efficiency tradeoffs.

D1.justification: v4 adds an explicit code-review link, identifies 8×H800 GPUs for timing measurements, separates filtering and training times, and states the default filtering threshold and replay ratio. Existing framework, learning-rate, batch-size, temperature, KL and prompt-template disclosures are retained; the link's availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Zhang et al. (2025), positioning reasoning-trajectory SFT findings as complementary to RFT's forgetting resistance without reasoning format. Appendix D adds references supporting the new datasets, models and replay comparison. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are preserved. Changes include localized related-work and RIF-RFT rewrites, new Appendix D subsections, removal of the former LLM-writing disclosure, and author/header edits; there is no extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Tables 6–11 substantially expand the visual presentation with text/model comparisons, replay and order results, a runtime breakdown and a threshold sweep. Figure 4 receives a revised gradient label and caption, and Table 3 moves alongside Table 4. The original benchmark plots and table structures otherwise remain.

improvement.justification: v2 supports broad conclusions mainly with one multimodal model configuration and data-retention evidence for efficiency. v4 adds text-only and additional-model evaluations, task-order checks, an evaluated replay comparator, and runtime measurements including filtering overhead, substantially strengthening empirical support and practical usefulness. The new filtering limitation improves balance. The mean-versus-maximum threshold inconsistency and absent uncertainty estimates remain limitations, but do not outweigh these substantial validation gains.
